evidence_excerpts: We propose an alternative to Bayesian NNs that is simple to implement, readily parallelizable, requires very little hyperparameter tuning, and yields high quality predictive uncertainty estimates.
requirements: Ctrl-World must train independently initialized or bootstrapped local arm-value predictors rather than duplicate a deterministic head after training.
Ensemble disagreement must be calibrated against held-out paired arm outcomes before it can gate execution.
failure_boundaries: An ensemble estimates epistemic uncertainty but does not by itself define an asymmetric harmful-routing objective or improve the adapter residual.
1612.01474v3.extraction_rationale: The abstract explicitly presents independently trainable, parallelizable predictors as a practical source of predictive uncertainty.

evidence_excerpts: In this paper we argue for the fundamental importance of the value distribution : the distribution of the random return received by a reinforcement learning agent.
This is in contrast to the common approach to reinforcement learning which models the expectation of this return, or value .
requirements: Each negative, zero, and positive Ctrl-World correction arm needs multiple future-regret observations or a justified empirical return distribution.
The routing rule must state which part of the return distribution represents harmful terminal and horizon risk.
failure_boundaries: Distributional value learning can be unstable in control and is not a finite-sample safety guarantee for an unseen rollout context.
1707.06887v1.extraction_rationale: The abstract explicitly replaces expected return with the full return distribution and connects that representation to risk-aware behavior.

evidence_excerpts: Traditionally, reinforcement learning algorithms average over this randomness to estimate the value function.
In this paper, we build on recent work advocating a distributional approach to reinforcement learning in which the distribution over returns is modeled explicitly instead of only estimating the mean.
requirements: The local value bank must retain per-seed or bootstrap future-regret samples instead of collapsing them into one mean label.
Quantiles must be evaluated for calibration and ordering separately for every correction arm.
failure_boundaries: Quantile regression models observed return variability but requires an additional treatment-specific uncertainty or calibration rule under context shift.
1710.10044v1.extraction_rationale: The abstract explicitly defines quantile regression as a way to model a long-term return distribution instead of its mean.

evidence_excerpts: This paper considers Safe Policy Improvement (SPI) in Batch Reinforcement Learning (Batch RL): from a fixed dataset and without direct access to the true environment, train a policy that is guaranteed to perform at least as well as the baseline policy used to collect the data.
Our approach, called SPI with Baseline Bootstrapping (SPIBB), is inspired by the knows-what-it-knows paradigm: it bootstraps the trained policy with the baseline when the uncertainty is high.
requirements: Zero correction must be the explicit baseline arm and remain exactly identical to the official Ctrl-World predictor.
The uncertainty set and minimum support rule must be frozen from development-only local arm outcomes.
failure_boundaries: SPIBB guarantees rely on a batch-RL setting and cannot be transferred as a theorem to a finite, non-Markov video-rollout bank; target-side promotion remains empirical.
1712.06924v5.extraction_rationale: The abstract explicitly defines a trainable batch policy that falls back to its data-collection baseline in high-uncertainty states.

evidence_excerpts: Rigorous guarantees about the performance of predictive algorithms are necessary in order to ensure their responsible use.
Previous work has largely focused on bounding the expected loss of a predictor, but this is not sufficient in many risk-sensitive applications where the distribution of errors is important.
requirements: The high-loss event must be defined by terminal interaction regression, harmful local routing, or horizon-slope regression rather than mean L1 alone.
Quantile-risk calibration data must remain development-only and preserve per-context grouping.
failure_boundaries: Tail-risk calibration certifies a selection rule but does not supply gradients that make the corrector's nonzero arms more useful.
2212.13629v1.extraction_rationale: The abstract explicitly argues that expected-loss bounds are inadequate for high-loss events and motivates quantile risk control.
